setting: Municipal pool locker room after swim practice
topic: Creating inclusion for a transgender teammate
summary: Kelda asks Theron how to support a trans teammate facing locker-room whispers.
plan: Kelda plans to have the team vote on whether to add a brief pronoun round during locker-room announcements, expecting that unanimous or majority approval will settle the matter and stop the whispers.
flaw: A vote puts the trans teammate's privacy and inclusion up for collective approval, which can out them or make them feel judged, and it won't stop whispers because majority rule doesn't change informal peer behavior.

setting: city procurement review room with bid binders
topic: evaluating low-bid proposals for parking garage repairs
summary: Stellan asks Marwa how to evaluate a low-bid proposal for parking garage repairs.
plan: Stellan plans to rank the low-bid proposals by simply picking the lowest total dollar figure in each binder, assuming the lowest number automatically reflects the best value for the garage repairs.
flaw: The lowest total bid may exclude required items like mobilization, traffic control, or concrete testing that appear as separate line items or alternates, so the apparent low number is not comparable across proposals until all mandatory scope items are added in.

setting: living room video setup with yarn baskets
topic: demonstrating knitting techniques for left-handed learners
summary: Jules asks Ioana for advice on filming a knitting tutorial for left-handed viewers.
plan: Jules plans to film the tutorial right-handed and simply flip the video horizontally in editing, assuming the mirrored footage will look exactly like a left-handed knitter working naturally.
flaw: Mirroring flips any text, logos, or on-screen labels in the frame so they read backwards, which is distracting or unreadable for viewers. It also reverses the direction of the yarn and the orientation of the stitches, so the result doesn't match how a left-handed knitter actually holds the needles and works.

summary: Adelina asks Yori for help arranging origami butterflies across a hospital room wall.
plan: Adelina plans to glue the paper butterflies directly onto the wall with strong craft adhesive in a dense cluster, believing that the more firmly they are attached and the closer they are grouped, the longer the display will last and the more calming the effect will be.
flaw: Strong glue will likely tear the delicate origami paper and damage the wall paint when the display is eventually removed, which matters in a hospital room that must be restored. A denser cluster also blocks the light and shadow play that makes a sparse arrangement feel soothing, and lightweight paper pieces are better hung or mounted with removable, gentle fasteners.

setting: shared photography studio beside charging stations
topic: choosing a backup strategy for high-volume photo archives
summary: Gwen asks Ryo for help selecting a backup strategy for a photographer collective.
plan: Gwen plans to have every photographer in the collective copy their edited final images to a shared external hard drive at the studio once a week, believing that this single drive serves as the collective's backup.
flaw: The flaw is that the drive sits in the same studio as the original working files, so a fire, flood, or theft would destroy both copies at once, and there is no off-site copy. It also only backs up edited finals, leaving raw files unbacked-up.

setting: cider mill processing room during harvest
topic: testing pasteurization temperature probes in cider production
summary: Hanneli asks Ciro how to test pasteurization temperature probes on a cider line.
plan: Hanneli plans to test the pasteurization temperature probes by pulling them from the line, bringing them to a rolling boil in a pot of water, and confirming they read 100°C before reinstalling them.
flaw: A probe calibrated in boiling water is checked at only one high point, and boiling water at her altitude may not be exactly 100°C; more importantly, a single-point check does not verify the probe's accuracy across the pasteurization range, which is where the readings actually matter.

topic: verifying allergen cleaning between production runs
summary: Belen asks Kareem how to verify allergen cleaning after switching granola flavors.
plan: Belen plans to verify allergen cleaning by swabbing the stainless steel surfaces after the washdown and sending those swabs for a general protein test, figuring that any leftover allergen residue will show up as protein.
flaw: A general protein test can be positive from ordinary food residues or cleaning chemicals and can also miss allergens that have been broken down or are present at low but still relevant levels, so it does not specifically confirm that the target allergen was removed.

topic: writing a hazard analysis for kombucha bottling
summary: Phoebe asks Hassan how to prepare a hazard analysis for a kombucha bottling line.
plan: Phoebe plans to base the hazard analysis for the kombucha bottling line on the finished-product micro specs alone, reasoning that if the bottled kombucha tests within limits, the process steps feeding it must be low-risk enough to leave out of the hazard analysis.
flaw: A hazard analysis has to evaluate each process step for biological, chemical, and physical hazards before deciding on controls; finished-product testing only samples a tiny fraction of output and won't reveal where contamination could be introduced, so it can't justify omitting steps from the analysis.
